view.lede: The Park, right-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (galloping), with the smaller of its two stand sides. A big, flat, galloping left- or right-handed oval with a long run-in and a straight mile, the teardrop shape the owner settled on for the kit Park (16 Nov: 'a little more teardrop / angular ... 2 chutes'). Dressed as a country galloping course.
notes: Newcastle, Redcar, Yarmouth, Salisbury, Chepstow, Ayr, Ffos Las, Nottingham, Leicester, Wetherby, Bath.
About 14.2f round, a 3.94f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Country galloping course: old small stands and pavilions clustered round the winning post, near the end of the straight, the crowd up to the rail, the festival in the infield opposite.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
